sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Imports for the fold-out map
sections.what: Brings in the React tools, the village drawing engine, the translated text, and the map labels.
sections.why: Lets the map draw its satellite thumbnails and show text in the chosen language.
sections.watch_out: The drawing engine must be ready before thumbnails appear, so a change to its loading order can leave the thumbnails blank.

sections.name: FoldedSurveyMap (part 1)
sections.title: Open state and background setup
sections.what: Keeps track of whether the map is open, whether the opening animation has finished, which pin is selected, and where the floating card sits. It takes the background picture once, and redraws the satellite thumbnails when the engine reports it is ready. It also cleans up that listener when the component leaves the screen.
sections.why: Keeps the map state in one place and makes sure the thumbnails redraw after the engine finishes loading.
sections.watch_out: Opening the map starts a timer of about one and a half seconds. The stylesheet must use the same length, or the settled state will arrive at the wrong moment.

sections.name: FoldedSurveyMap: if
sections.title: Pin click and card placement
sections.what: When a pin is tapped, the code either hides the card if the same pin is tapped again, or places the card near the pin and shows it. The card position is chosen so it stays on the screen. Tapping the satellite pin also redraws the thumbnails after a short delay.
sections.why: Keeps the floating card visible for pins near the edge of the map and keeps the satellite thumbnails up to date.
sections.watch_out: The short delay before redrawing is a guess that helps the thumbnails appear after the card opens. Changing the layout may require a new delay.

sections.name: FoldedSurveyMap (part 3)
sections.title: Map layout and cover
sections.what: Builds the card with a header and toggle button. The map is three panels that fold like paper. The left panel has a cover with a title, a compass rose and a note with a mauza and khata. Clicking anywhere on the map opens it when closed.
sections.why: Gives the fold-out look and invites the user to open the map.
sections.watch_out: The cover text mauza and khata numbers are typed in, so they will not match a different demo or real case.

sections.name: FoldedSurveyMap (part 4)
sections.title: Tappable pins and floating card start
sections.what: Places three pins at fixed spots on the map and wires each to the pin click logic. Starts the floating card, which is hidden until a pin is active and can be closed with a button.
sections.why: Lets the user explore evidence by tapping parts of the map.
sections.watch_out: Pin positions are typed percentages, so they must match where the features appear in the picture.

sections.name: FoldedSurveyMap (part 5)
sections.title: Contents of each floating card tab
sections.what: The area tab shows a count of 3 of 4, three acreage values, and a link to the differences section. The official tab shows zero records and a button that shows a demo message. The satellite tab shows two thumbnails and a button that shows a demo message.
sections.why: Gives a short explanation of each evidence type, with demo messages where real search or comparison is not available.
sections.watch_out: The count and acreage values are fixed in the code, not calculated, so the card can show figures that do not match the real parcel.

sections.name: FoldedSurveyMap (part 6)
sections.title: Map tabs for area, official records and satellite
sections.what: Finishes the folded survey map card. It shows three tabs: area sources with a button to see the area comparison, an official-style record tab showing a count of 0 with a search button, and a satellite tab with two image placeholders and a button to view change. The two demo buttons show a short notice saying the feature is not available in the demo.
sections.why: Likely reason: the demo does not connect to real search or image comparison, so the buttons explain that instead of doing nothing. Reason not stated in the code.
sections.watch_out: The two satellite canvases are filled by code elsewhere through refs, so removing those refs leaves them blank, and the official count of 0 is typed in directly rather than read from data.

summary: An animated fold-out survey map card that shows the evidence for a parcel with three tappable pins for area, official records and satellite views.
purpose: Shows the land evidence in a playful but clear way, letting the owner open the map and tap for details.
why: Likely reason: the fold animation makes the evidence feel like a paper survey. Reason not stated in the code.
how: Starts closed. Opening the map starts an animation timer, after which the map is marked as settled. Tapping a pin places a floating card near it, and that card shows area figures, the official record count, or satellite thumbnails. Closing clears the selected pin. The satellite thumbnails are redrawn from the village engine when it is ready.
inputs: Optional callbacks for a toast message and for jumping to the differences section, plus the current language from the locale context.
outputs: A card with a fold-out map, pins, a floating detail card, and a toggle button.
risks: Many area and count figures are typed in, so they do not come from the real parcel data. The animation timer must match the animation length in the stylesheet. Pin positions are fixed percentages that must line up with the picture.
debug: If the map does not open, check the open state and the toggle button. If thumbnails are blank, check the village engine and the ready callback. If the card goes off screen, check the position values for the pin.
